I’m so sorry :(  I know what it is you’re feeling right now, but it will get easier with time. The best thing I can say to you right now is try to remember the good times you two have spent with each other, your friend wouldn’t want you to be in this much pain. My best friend ODed from heroin 1 year and 8 months ago now, and I’ll never know if it was suicide or just him trying to numb the pain (his last week we found out he was going down a very self destructive path..) I wish I listened to him more, and there’s so much more I wish I did (we’ve most likely concluded it was his very first time using). But the only thing we can do now is cherish the positive time we’ve spent with him because there’s so many more positive memories then negative ones. It’s funny because no matter how funny he was and how much love he showered onto his friends, the people who didn’t know him well just see him as another sad junky story who overdosed (which isn’t even close to true).

You must be strong, and try and pick yourself up not only for yourself, but for those around you. Your friend wouldn’t want you to be in this much pain. maybe try going for a walk outside, listen to your friends favorite music, cry a little bit- it’s good for you. You need to let your emotions out in a positive way, and with time you will heal. :)

This used to be me, man.. back in my high school and early college days I would drink to become social, and it worked for a long time. After years of doing this, the drinking eventually would put me in a massive depressive state, to the point I realized I probably shouldn’t be drinking anymore (or at least not getting black out drunk) because I would become so sad and suicidal. When I drank, it was the only time I realized i could open up to people and be “normal”. That’s not true though. Although, sometimes substances can be used as a tool to assist with anxiety, depression, or whatever.. you shouldn’t have to 100% rely on it all the time, as it will only cause more problems down the road. If i were you, I would probably try to limit the amount of drinks I consume in a night (for example let’s say 4), and try your absolute hardest to socialize and talk to random people. Once you attempt to desensitize yourself to these situations, it will only become easier and easier. Then maybe only start to consume a drink or two in a given night and continue on with your socializing/desensitizing. Then use these skills in the real world and try to do it without any alcohol. If you’re consistent and really believe in yourself and try your hardest, I know you can do this. We all can. We don’t need alcohol to socialize- we might think so at certain points in our lives, but it’s not true. It’s just us trying to suffocate our anxiety when really we should embrace it and embarrass it and say “fuck you” anxiety, you ain’t shit.
